messages:
Ravi: quick alert  found a few sampled request bodies in S3 debug-bucket with raw phone numbers (US format). Only 7 items but still bad.
Nina: where did they come from? route/tenant?
Ravi: burst-routing -> debug-forwarder -> us-east-1. Tenants are internal QA and one customer staging. The console sampling for burst routes was at 2% this morning.
Tara: Any idea how they slipped past scrub? we run phone regex in the scrubber.
Ravi: looks like the parts were HTML attachments, base64-encoded, and small-chunk fast-path avoided the structured parse. snippet we pulled:
```text
{"attachments": [{"content_type": "text/html", "data": "PGgyPkNvbnRhY3Q6IDxmYXI+KzE4MDAtNTU1LTAxMjM8L2Zhci4+"}]}
# base64 decodes to: "Contact: +1800-555-0123"
```
Nina: Ugh. Same fast-path gap as earlier multipart/base64 issues. Which deploy touched burst-forwarding?
Ravi: rollout id rf-2026-burst-forward v3.2.4 yesterday. Console shows sampling toggle enabled for burst routes.
ops-bot: alert created: INC-6123 -> https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-6123 (severity: P2)
Tara: Immediate mitigation: lower burst-route sampling to 0.1% and set inspect.capture_level=meta_only for the burst-forwarder in us-east-1. That avoids bodies while keeping trace ids.
Nina: prefer tweak over full rollback. Any downside for debugging latency anomalies?
Ravi: we'll lose payloads but maintain timing and headers. We can re-run targeted synthetic traffic if needed.
Tara: For the fix: (1) ensure scrub runs pre-routing for all ingest paths including fast-path markers; (2) add a lightweight base64 quick-scan buffer that decodes first N bytes and runs phone/email regex; (3) add unit+e2e that simulates chunked base64 attachments.
Nina: also add a console rule: any sampled object that contains digit patterns of length 10+ triggers a low-severity log and hides full body automatically. We already have something similar for SSNs but not for phone patterns.
Ravi: filing INF-4899 with repro, logs and proposed patch: https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-4899
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: sampling-reduction burst-forwarder us-east-1 -> 1741238400 (ETA 8m)
Tara: I'll start the scrub refactor PR. Plan: move scrub to ingest head, add decode-safety guard (max 128KB), and a fallback heuristic to redact digit groups before any forwarding.
Nina: I'll update runbooks and add a short dashboard panel: "sampled bodies with patterns" with a 24h retention for quick triage.
Ravi: after patch, propose a canary with single tenant at 0.5% sample and two-hour watch. If green, restore to previous sampling.
Tara: ETA for PR? aiming EOD, will request review from Nina/Ravi.
Nina: thumbs. Also we should audit other forwarders (minidaemon, debug-burst, prefetch) for the same fast-path bypass.
Ravi: noted, adding checklist to the ticket. Closing once rollback completes and patch is merged.
